unit: Ch 14: TDS and TCS under GST
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Overview and Deductors of Tax at Source (TDS)
explain: Tax Deduction at Source (TDS) requires specified recipients to deduct tax when making payments to suppliers of taxable goods or services.
It creates an audit trail, prevents tax evasion, and ensures regular revenue inflow to the Government.
Statutory deductors include Central and State Government departments or establishments, local authorities, and governmental agencies.
Notified deductors under clause (d) include Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and societies set up by Government or Local Authorities.
Boards, authorities, or bodies established by Parliament, State Legislature, or Government with 51% or more equity or control are also deductors.
Registered persons receiving metal scrap (Chapters 72 to 81 of Customs Tariff) from other registered persons must also deduct TDS.
Prescribed Defence Ministry authorities are exempt from TDS deduction requirements.

flow.title: Steps to Identify a Mandatory TDS Deductor
steps: Identify recipient receiving taxable supply
Check if recipient is Govt department/establishment
Check if recipient is Local Authority or Agency
Check if PSU, Govt Society, or 51%+ Govt Body
Check if registered buyer receiving metal scrap
If yes, recipient must deduct TDS on payment

topics.example: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), a body set up by Parliament with 100% Government control, awards a road building contract to a private contractor. NHAI must act as a TDS deductor.
remember: 51% or more Government equity or control is required for notified boards or bodies to be deductors.
Registered persons purchasing metal scrap from registered suppliers are mandatory deductors regardless of entity type.
mistakes: Assuming all societies or private companies must deduct TDS without checking if they have 51%+ Government control or purchase metal scrap.

quiz.q: Which of the following entities is NOT a mandatory TDS deductor under Section 51?
o: Private Limited Company with no Government control or scrap purchases
quiz.why: Private companies without Government control or metal scrap transactions are not notified deductors under Section 51.

quiz.q: What minimum percentage of Government equity or control makes an authority set up by Parliament a TDS deductor?
quiz.why: Circular No. 76/50/2018 clarifies that 51% or more participation by way of equity or control is required.

topics.title: TDS Threshold Limit, Value of Supply, and Rate of Deduction
explain: TDS deduction is mandatory only when the total value of taxable supply under a single contract exceeds ₹ 2,50,000.
For threshold evaluation, the contract value excludes CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST, and cess indicated in the invoice.
Standard rate of TDS under CGST Act is 1% CGST plus 1% SGST (total 2%) for intra-State supplies.
Rate of TDS under IGST Act (via Section 20) is 2% IGST for inter-State supplies.
Even if individual billing invoices are less than ₹ 2,50,000, TDS is deducted on each payment if the total contract value exceeds ₹ 2,50,000.

flow.title: Process to Evaluate TDS Applicability on Payments
steps: Check total taxable supply value under contract
Exclude GST taxes and cess from contract value
Is total contract value over ₹ 2,50,000?
Determine supply type: Intra-State vs Inter-State
Intra-State: Deduct 1% CGST + 1% SGST
Inter-State: Deduct 2% IGST

topics.example: A State Government department enters into a single maintenance contract worth ₹ 3,00,000 (excluding GST) with a vendor, billed quarterly at ₹ 75,000. TDS @ 2% (1% CGST + 1% SGST) must be deducted from each quarterly payment because total contract value exceeds ₹ 2,50,000.
remember: The ₹ 2.5 lakh threshold applies to the total contract value, not individual invoice values.
Tax rate is 1% CGST + 1% SGST (Total 2%) for intra-State or 2% IGST for inter-State supplies.
mistakes: Including CGST, SGST, or IGST amounts when determining whether the contract value exceeds ₹ 2,50,000.

quiz.q: What is the threshold contract value for TDS deduction under Section 51?
quiz.why: TDS is required when the total value of taxable supply under a contract exceeds ₹ 2,50,000 exclusive of GST.

quiz.q: What rate of TDS is deducted under the CGST Act for intra-State supplies?
quiz.why: Section 51(1) mandates 1% under CGST Act (which is matched by 1% under SGST Act, making total intra-State TDS 2%).

topics.title: Situations Where TDS is NOT Deducted
topics.section: Proviso to Section 51(1) of CGST Act
explain: No TDS is deducted when Location of Supplier and Place of Supply are in State A, while the Recipient is registered in State B.
This exception exists because transferring intra-State TDS (State A taxes) to the cash ledger of a recipient registered in State B is not feasible.
Supplies made by one Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) to another PSU do not attract TDS (except for metal scrap supplies).
Supplies between specified deductors under Section 51(1)(a)-(d) are exempt from TDS (except metal scrap transactions).
Exempt supplies and supplies covered under reverse charge mechanism do not attract TDS.

flow.title: Testing Exception Rules for TDS Exemption
steps: Check if supply is from PSU to PSU
Check if transaction is between notified deductors
If yes (and not metal scrap), apply NO TDS rule
Identify Location of Supplier and Place of Supply
Identify Recipient Registration State
If Supplier & POS in State A but Recipient in State B, apply NO TDS

topics.example: A local authority registered in Punjab (State B) engages a contractor for work executed in Haryana (State A), where the contractor is registered. Since Location of Supplier and Place of Supply are both in Haryana, but Recipient is in Punjab, no TDS is deducted.
remember: Location of Supplier + Place of Supply in State A, Recipient in State B = NO TDS.
Transactions between PSUs attract NO TDS unless the supply relates to metal scrap.
mistakes: Assuming TDS applies whenever a Government department makes a payment, ignoring the location of recipient proviso.

quiz.q: Under the proviso to Section 51(1), in which situation is NO tax deducted at source?
o: Supplier, Place of Supply, and Recipient are all in State A
Supplier is in State A, Place of Supply is State B, Recipient is State B
Supplier and Place of Supply are in State A, but Recipient is registered in State B
Supplier is in Union Territory 1 and Recipient is in Union Territory 1
quiz.why: When Location of Supplier and Place of Supply are in one State/UT while Recipient is registered in another State/UT, no TDS is made.

quiz.q: Is TDS deductible on a supply of general goods worth ₹ 10,00,000 from BHEL (a PSU) to NTPC (another PSU)?
o: No, supplies between PSUs are exempt from TDS
quiz.why: Supplies from one PSU to another PSU are specifically exempt from TDS deduction (except metal scrap).

topics.title: TDS Compliance Procedures and Accounting
explain: Deductors must obtain compulsory GST registration under Rule 12, granted by the Proper Officer within 3 working days.
The tax deducted at source must be remitted to the Government within 10 days after the end of the month of deduction.
The deductor files a monthly return in Form GSTR-7 under Section 39(3), which automatically generates Form GSTR-7A (TDS Certificate).
The deducted tax amount is directly credited to the Electronic Cash Ledger of the deductee (supplier).
Failure to remit TDS attracts interest under Section 50. Excess or erroneous deductions can be refunded under Section 54.

flow.title: TDS Remittance and Credit Flow Lifecycle
steps: Deductor registers under Rule 12 within 3 days
Deducts tax at time of payment or credit
Deposits TDS to Govt by 10th of next month
Files monthly return in Form GSTR-7
System generates Form GSTR-7A certificate
Amount reflects in supplier's Electronic Cash Ledger

topics.example: A Government department deducts ₹ 40,000 TDS in July. It must deposit this amount to the Government Treasury by August 10th and file Form GSTR-7 so the vendor can claim credit in their Electronic Cash Ledger.
remember: Due date for TDS deposit and Form GSTR-7 filing: 10th day of the succeeding month.
Form GSTR-7A is the TDS certificate generated online after GSTR-7 return filing.
TDS credit flows into the supplier's Electronic Cash Ledger (not Credit Ledger).
mistakes: Confusing Electronic Cash Ledger with Electronic Credit Ledger when accounting for TDS credit claimed by the supplier.

quiz.q: By what date must tax deducted at source under Section 51 be deposited to the Government?
quiz.why: Section 51(2) requires the deductor to pay the deducted amount to the Government within 10 days after the end of the month.

quiz.q: Which form is generated as a TDS certificate for the deductee?
quiz.why: Form GSTR-7A is the TDS Certificate issued based on the return filed in Form GSTR-7.

topics.title: Collection of Tax at Source (TCS) under Section 52 - Scope and Rates
explain: Tax Collection at Source (TCS) is collected by an Electronic Commerce Operator (ECO) on net taxable supplies made through its platform by third-party suppliers.
TCS applies only when the ECO collects consideration from the customer on behalf of the supplier.
ECO must not be an agent acting on its own account.
If a person sells their own products through their own website, TCS provisions do not apply (normal GST applies).
Rate of TCS under CGST Act is 0.25% CGST plus 0.25% SGST (total 0.5%) on intra-State net taxable supplies.
Rate of TCS under IGST Act (via Section 20) is 0.5% IGST on inter-State net taxable supplies.

flow.title: Evaluating TCS Applicability on E-Commerce Transactions
steps: Check if entity operates an e-commerce platform
Check if goods/services belong to third-party sellers
Check if ECO collects consideration from buyer
If yes, ECO must collect TCS
Calculate net value of taxable supplies
Apply 0.5% TCS (0.25%+0.25% intra, 0.5% inter)

topics.example: ShopKart, an ECO, facilitates ₹ 50,00,000 intra-State sales of electronics for third-party registered sellers and collects payment from buyers. ShopKart must collect TCS @ 0.5% (0.25% CGST + 0.25% SGST), totaling ₹ 25,000.
remember: TCS applies only when the ECO collects payment for third-party supplies.
TCS Rate: 0.25% CGST + 0.25% SGST (0.5% total) or 0.5% IGST.
mistakes: Levying TCS when a seller sells goods on their own website without any third-party operator involvement.

quiz.q: Who is mandated to collect tax at source under Section 52 of the CGST Act?
o: Electronic Commerce Operator (not being an agent)
Supplier selling directly on their own website
quiz.why: Section 52(1) mandates Electronic Commerce Operators (not being agents) to collect TCS on net taxable supplies made through them.

quiz.q: What is the total TCS rate (CGST + SGST) applicable on intra-State taxable supplies made through an ECO?
quiz.why: The notified TCS rate for intra-State supplies is 0.25% CGST and 0.25% SGST, totaling 0.5%.

topics.title: Net Value of Taxable Supplies & Section 9(5) Exclusions
topics.section: Section 52(1) Explanation & Section 9(5) of CGST Act
explain: Net Value of Taxable Supplies = Aggregate value of taxable supplies of goods/services made by registered suppliers through ECO minus taxable supplies returned to suppliers during the month.
Net value excludes taxes (CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST, cess) indicated in the invoice.
Services notified under Section 9(5) are EXCLUDED from the net value calculation for TCS purposes.

Under Section 9(5), the ECO itself is liable to pay tax as deemed supplier (e.g., radio-taxi, omnibus except companies, hotel accommodation by unregistered suppliers, housekeeping by unregistered suppliers, restaurant services, local delivery by unregistered suppliers).
If a hotel is already registered under Section 22(1), Section 9(5) does not apply to the ECO, so normal TCS @ 0.5% is collected by the ECO.

flow.title: Calculation of Net Value of Taxable Supplies for TCS
steps: Sum aggregate gross taxable supplies made through ECO
Subtract value of sales returns in that month
Exclude services notified under Section 9(5)
Exclude GST tax and cess amounts from invoice
Arrive at Net Value of Taxable Supplies
Multiply Net Value by applicable TCS rate

topics.example: QuickMart facilitates ₹ 5,00,000 intra-State sales of electronic goods and ₹ 2,00,000 cab ride bookings (notified under Section 9(5)). The ₹ 2,00,000 cab rides are excluded from TCS calculation because QuickMart pays GST directly under Section 9(5). TCS @ 0.5% is collected only on ₹ 5,00,000 (i.e., ₹ 2,500).
remember: Sales returns within the same month are subtracted from gross supplies to find Net Value.
Section 9(5) services (where ECO pays GST directly) are completely excluded from TCS.
mistakes: Including Section 9(5) notified services (like Ola cab rides or Zomato food delivery) in net taxable supply for TCS collection.

quiz.q: Which of the following items is EXCLUDED when calculating 'net value of taxable supplies' for TCS under Section 52?
o: Goods returned by customers during the month
GST taxes and cess indicated in invoice
quiz.why: Net value excludes sales returns, taxes/cess, and Section 9(5) notified services.

quiz.q: Why are cab aggregator services (radio-taxis) excluded from TCS calculation by an ECO?
o: They are completely exempt from GST
The ECO pays GST directly as deemed supplier under Section 9(5)
Only local authorities can pay tax on cab rides
quiz.why: Radio-taxi services are notified under Section 9(5), making the ECO directly liable to pay GST as if it were the supplier; hence no TCS applies.

topics.title: Compliance Procedures for TCS (Deposit, Statements, and Notice)
explain: ECO must obtain compulsory registration under Section 24 / Rule 12 (granted within 3 working days).
TCS collected by the ECO must be deposited to the Government Treasury within 10 days after the end of the month.
ECO must file a monthly electronic statement in Form GSTR-8 within 10 days after the end of the month.
ECO must also file an Annual Statement in Form GSTR-9B on or before 31st December following the end of the financial year.
Omissions or incorrect particulars in Form GSTR-8 can be rectified up to 30th November following the end of the FY or actual date of filing Annual Statement, whichever is earlier.

An officer not below the rank of Deputy Commissioner can issue a notice to ECO seeking details of supplies or warehouse stock; ECO must furnish details within 15 working days or face a penalty up to ₹ 25,000 under Section 52(14).

flow.title: TCS Compliance and Reporting Lifecycle
steps: ECO registers under Rule 12 within 3 working days
Collects TCS on monthly net taxable supplies
Deposits TCS to Govt Treasury by 10th of next month
Files Monthly Statement in Form GSTR-8 by 10th of next month
Supplier claims TCS credit in Electronic Cash Ledger
Files Annual Statement in Form GSTR-9B by 31st December

topics.example: BuyBazaar collects TCS during July. It must deposit the tax collected into the Government Treasury and submit Form GSTR-8 online on or before August 10th.
remember: Monthly TCS Statement: Form GSTR-8 (due by 10th of succeeding month).
Annual TCS Statement: Form GSTR-9B (due by 31st December following FY).
Deadline to respond to Section 52(12) notice: 15 working days (penalty up to ₹ 25,000).
mistakes: Confusing Form GSTR-7 (monthly return for TDS) with Form GSTR-8 (monthly statement for TCS).

quiz.q: Which monthly electronic statement must be filed by an ECO collecting TCS under Section 52?
quiz.why: Form GSTR-8 is the monthly statement required to be furnished by every ECO collecting tax at source under Section 52(4).

quiz.q: What is the time limit for an ECO to respond to a notice served by a Deputy Commissioner under Section 52(12)?
quiz.why: Section 52(13) mandates that the required information must be furnished within 15 working days of the date of service of notice.
